line: **Siberian Ibex (Asiatic Ibex):** wild goat native to **Central Asia**; the **Himalayan Ibex** is its subspecies; found in J&K, **Ladakh** and HP on rocky mountain zones; IUCN **Near Threatened**, WPA Schedule I.
**Bishnois:** founded by **Guru Jambheshwar (Jambhoji)** in Rajasthan, **1485**; the name comes from 'Bis' (20) + 'Noi' (9) = his **29 principles** on God, nature and ethical living.

mcq.s: The Bishnoi community was founded by whom?
mcq.x: Guru Jambheshwar (Jambhoji) founded the Bishnoi sect in Rajasthan in 1485 with 29 principles.

line: **Laurentian type (cool temperate eastern margin):** cold climate with moderate summer rain (about **40 inches**); natural vegetation **mixed forests** (coniferous and deciduous); **fishing** is its most outstanding economic activity.

mcq.s: The 'Laurentian type' of climate is found on which margin of the continents in the cool temperate belt?
mcq.x: Laurentian type = cool temperate eastern margin climate with moderate summer rain and mixed forests.

line: **Cape Sao Roque:** the 'shoulder' of **Brazil** divides the west-flowing equatorial current into the **Cayenne Current** (flows north-west) and the **Brazilian Current** (flows south-west).

mcq.s: The 'shoulder' of Brazil at Cape Sao Roque divides the west-flowing equatorial current into the Brazilian Current and which other current?
mcq.x: Cape Sao Roque splits it into the Cayenne Current (north-west) and the Brazilian Current (south-west).

line: **Amhara:** region of **Ethiopia** often in the news (Anatolia – Turkey).
**Nile – dams and tributaries:** **Lake Nasser** is the reservoir of the **Aswan High Dam** (Egypt); main tributaries White Nile, Blue Nile and **Atbarah**; cities Khartoum, Atbara, Cairo.

mcq.s: Lake Nasser is the reservoir formed by which dam?
mcq.x: Lake Nasser on the Nile lies behind the Aswan High Dam in Egypt.

line: **Weddell Sea:** in the Southern Ocean, south of the Atlantic and east of the **Antarctic Peninsula**; much of the world's **cold oceanic bottom water** originates here; **Seymour Island** lies in it.
**Volcanic spine / plug:** very viscous lava forms a spine or plug at the crater, e.g. **Mt. Pelee (Martinique)**; resistant plugs may survive long erosion, e.g. **Puy de Dome (France)**.
**Till / drift plains:** glacial deposits spread in gently undulating sheets; some boulder clay plains, e.g. **East Anglia** and the northern **Mid-West of the USA**, form rich arable lands.
**Karst lake:** lakes in a polje without surface outlet cover the floor in wet periods and shrink by seepage in dry periods, e.g. **Lake Scutari** (Yugoslavia).
**Solution lakes:** many **meres of Cheshire** (England) formed by subsidence as underlying **rock salt** was removed in solution, and also by salt mining.
**Man-made lakes:** ornamental lakes such as Lake Gardens (Kuala Lumpur) and **Taiping Lakes**; **tin mining** in West Malaysia has created numerous lakes.

line: **Dhodia:** tribe of **Gujarat**, also in Rajasthan, Maharashtra and MP.
**Coalgate scam:** from 2004 coal blocks were allocated to private firms for **captive mining** **without competitive bidding** (2004-2009), marred by corruption.
**Niobium:** critical mineral for **clean technologies** and advanced manufacturing; reserves **not available** in India.
**Automobile centres:** Germany – **Stuttgart** and **Wolfsburg** (Mercedes-Benz, Porsche, **Volkswagen**); UK – **Coventry** and Birmingham; Brazil – **Sao Paulo** and Curitiba.

mcq.s: Wolfsburg, home of Volkswagen, is an automobile centre in which country?
mcq.x: Stuttgart and Wolfsburg in Germany host Mercedes-Benz, Porsche and Volkswagen.

line: **Chechnya:** a republic in south-western **Russia**, on the northern slopes of the **Greater Caucasus**.
**Mayotte:** **French** territory in the **Indian Ocean**; struck by Cyclone **Chido** (Dec 2024, strongest in 90 years) and Cyclone **Dikeledi** (Jan 2025).

line: **North American Cordillera:** a chain of mountain ranges that begins with the **Alaska Range** and the **Brooks Range**.

**Dardic tribes:** **Brokpa**, Drokpa and Shin speak **Dardic** (Indo-Aryan) languages; Brokpa ('Dard Aryans') of **Ladakh** claim descent from **Alexander**; Drokpa – Drass (Kargil); Shin – **Gurez Valley** (J&K).
**Hakki Pikki:** semi-nomadic tribe of **Karnataka**, traditionally **bird catchers** and hunters; believed to have come from Gujarat and Rajasthan, migrating to Karnataka via **Andhra Pradesh**.

mcq.s: Hakki Pikki, a semi-nomadic tribe of traditional bird catchers, lives mainly in which state?
mcq.x: Hakki Pikki are a semi-nomadic bird-catcher tribe of Karnataka, believed to have migrated from Gujarat and Rajasthan via Andhra Pradesh.

line: **NTCWPC (National Technology Centre for Ports, Waterways and Coasts):** set up at **IIT Chennai** under the **Sagarmala** scheme; technological arm of the **MoPSW** for the port sector.

mcq.s: The National Technology Centre for Ports, Waterways and Coasts (NTCWPC) was set up under which scheme?
mcq.x: NTCWPC was established at IIT Chennai under the Sagarmala scheme as the technological arm of the MoPSW.

line: **Hindustan Zinc smelters:** Chanderiya, Dariba and **Debari** (Rajasthan); Debari lies close to the **Rampura Agucha** zinc mine, with lead concentrate from Rajpura Dariba.
**Kuruvai:** short-duration (**90-120 days**) high-yielding paddy season of **Tamil Nadu**, June to September; **Samba** is the second main paddy season.

mcq.s: 'Kuruvai' and 'Samba' are paddy cultivation seasons of which state?
mcq.x: Kuruvai (June-September, 90-120 day paddy) and Samba are the main paddy seasons of Tamil Nadu.

line: **Paleogene Period (65-23 mya):** followed the Cretaceous; the **Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction** (Fifth Extinction, 66 mya) came with **Deccan Traps** eruptions and a meteor impact – **Chicxulub Crater** (Yucatan, Mexico).

mcq.s: The Chicxulub Crater, linked with the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction, is in which country?
mcq.x: The Chicxulub Crater is on the Yucatan Peninsula, Mexico.

line: **Partial solar eclipse (penumbra):** the Sun and Moon are not exactly in line with the Earth and the Moon only partly hides the Sun; seen from a large part of the Earth outside the annular or total track.
**Nova Scotia:** fertile **Annapolis valley** – world's most renowned apple region; fishing ports **Halifax** and **Yarmouth**; St. John's (Newfoundland) is the headquarters of Grand Banks fishing.
**Smallest countries of mainland Africa:** Gambia, **Eswatini (Swaziland)**, Djibouti, Rwanda and Burundi; smallest overall: Seychelles, Sao Tome and Principe, Mauritius, Comoros.
**Sanetti Plateau:** in south-eastern **Ethiopia's Bale Range**, mostly within **Bale Mountains NP**; formed by successive outpourings of **lava**.
**Isthmus of Panama:** formed by **subduction of the Pacific-Farallon Plate** beneath the **Caribbean** and **South American** plates, forming a volcanic arc.
**Potomac River:** rises at Green Spring, **West Virginia**; falls into **Chesapeake Bay** (Atlantic); **Washington, D.C.** lies on it.
**Little (Small) Prespa Lake:** on the **Greece–Albania** border, now turned into swamps or dried up; Great Prespa Lake is shared by Albania, Greece and **North Macedonia**.
**Murrumbidgee River (~1,485 km):** right-bank tributary of the **Murray**; rises on the western slopes of the Great Dividing Range (NSW); its basin gives over **50% of Australia's rice**.
**Komodo Dragon:** native to **Indonesia** (Komodo islands).
**Well-known constellations:** **Orion** (hunter), **Ursa Major** (Great Bear, Big Dipper, Saptarishi), Ursa Minor, **Cassiopeia** and Leo Major.
